title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #1

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a map of a village, the church is to the east of the school. On the map, where is the church drawn? (1 mark)
   A. On the left of the school
   B. On the right of the school
   C. Above the school
   D. Below the school

2. What do we call the smaller parts into which a sub-county is divided? (1 mark)
   A. Plateaus
   B. Continents
   C. Oceans
   D. Wards

3. Which ocean is found on the south-eastern side of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Pacific Ocean
   B. Arctic Ocean
   C. Atlantic Ocean
   D. Indian Ocean

4. Which of these counties has a coast on the Indian Ocean? (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru
   B. Kitui
   C. Kilifi
   D. Nyeri

5. Which county contains the capital city of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Kisumu
   C. Kitui
   D. Nakuru

6. What do we call describing where a county is by naming the places around it? (1 mark)
   A. Scale
   B. Rainfall
   C. Relative location
   D. Population

7. Where does a river usually start? (1 mark)
   A. In a lake
   B. On the beach
   C. On high land
   D. In the desert

8. Which of these is a way of caring for a river? (1 mark)
   A. Planting trees along its banks
   B. Washing cars in it
   C. Cutting trees at the bank
   D. Throwing rubbish into it

9. During the dry season herders in dry areas often do what? (1 mark)
   A. Plant maize
   B. Sell umbrellas
   C. Collect rainwater
   D. Move animals to find water and grass

10. Which disease can spread more easily in wet weather because mosquitoes breed in puddles? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Broken leg
   C. Toothache
   D. Malaria

11. Why do farmers plan their work using seasons? (1 mark)
   A. Seasons decide the colour of soil
   B. Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
   C. Seasons decide school holidays only
   D. Seasons tell the price of clothes

12. Which symbol on a weather chart shows rain? (1 mark)
   A. A thermometer
   B. A yellow sun
   C. A cloud with lines falling from it
   D. A plain cloud

13. Which of these actions helps to conserve a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Climbing on old walls
   B. Reporting anyone who damages it
   C. Leaving litter
   D. Breaking off small pieces

14. A tailor makes uniforms and a farmer buys them. What does the tailor need from the farmer? (1 mark)
   A. Cloth from the moon
   B. A tractor for sewing
   C. Nothing at all
   D. Food or money from selling food

15. Why do health workers depend on farmers? (1 mark)
   A. Farmers grow the food they eat
   B. Farmers make medicine
   C. Farmers keep records
   D. Farmers build hospitals

16. Which pattern describes people living along a road or river in a line? (1 mark)
   A. Clustered
   B. Linear
   C. Scattered
   D. Circular

17. Which game is played with seeds or stones moved between holes in a board? (1 mark)
   A. Bao
   B. Netball
   C. Football
   D. Athletics

18. What are school rules? (1 mark)
   A. Lunch
   B. Games
   C. Instructions on what we should and should not do
   D. Songs

19. Which words help to tell a history in order? (1 mark)
   A. Big, small, tall
   B. Red, blue, green
   C. Up, down, left
   D. First, then, later, today

20. Which activity earns money from visitors to game parks and beaches? (1 mark)
   A. Tourism
   B. Fishing
   C. Quarrying
   D. Mining

21. Which of these economic activities is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A crop of maize
   B. A fish
   C. Teaching
   D. A stone

22. Which factor makes a place suitable for a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Good roads and nearby workers
   B. No water
   C. No workers
   D. No roads

23. What should you do when visiting a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Touch all machines
   C. Run around
   D. Stay with the group and not touch machines

24. Which of these is a benefit of industries? (1 mark)
   A. They close schools
   B. They remove roads
   C. They stop trade
   D. They provide jobs

25. What is personal protective equipment used for? (1 mark)
   A. To protect a person from harm
   B. To slow down work
   C. To hide
   D. To make noise

26. Which action shows cooperation? (1 mark)
   A. Fighting
   B. Sharing tasks in a group
   C. Copying others
   D. Doing nothing

27. You find a lost pencil that belongs to a classmate. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Keep it
   C. Return it to the owner
   D. Sell it

28. Which is a benefit of good citizenship in school? (1 mark)
   A. The school is safe and orderly
   B. Property is broken
   C. Less learning
   D. More fights

29. What is a citizen? (1 mark)
   A. A member of a country or community with rights and duties
   B. A type of school
   C. A visitor who never returns
   D. A kind of law

30. Which of these is a right of a school citizen? (1 mark)
   A. To bully others
   B. To learn in a safe place
   C. To break rules
   D. To steal

31. What is a conflict? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A holiday
   C. A book
   D. A disagreement or quarrel

32. Which law forbids child labour and FGM in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Only school rules
   B. Only a poster
   C. The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act
   D. Nothing forbids it

33. What is female genital mutilation? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. A kind of school
   C. A kind of sport
   D. Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal

34. Which of these can cause child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Enough food
   B. Good schools
   C. Kind neighbours
   D. Poverty and harmful beliefs

35. What does majority mean? (1 mark)
   A. The larger number of votes
   B. No votes
   C. The smaller number of votes
   D. A tie

36. What is the meaning of composition of a group? (1 mark)
   A. The song of the group
   B. The people or parts that make up the group
   C. The size of the room
   D. The colour of the group

37. Which of these is a way of participating in the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring elections
   B. Voting for leaders
   C. Breaking rules
   D. Laughing at leaders

38. Which action shows good leadership? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping all the food
   B. Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   C. Giving only to friends
   D. Hiding the food

39. How often are governors elected? (1 mark)
   A. Every year
   B. Every five years
   C. Every month
   D. Every twenty years

40. Who approves the governor's choice of county executive committee members? (1 mark)
   A. The county assembly
   B. The teachers
   C. The village elder
   D. The chief

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain how a county with a big lake and a dry plain could earn a living from both. (4 marks)

42. In a class election, Maria got 14 votes, Juma got 9 votes and 2 papers were spoilt. How many pupils voted? Who won? Show working. (3 marks)

43. Explain how a class representative helps classmates. (3 marks)

44. Explain what a child should do if someone makes them feel unsafe. (3 marks)

45. What is the difference between a lake and a river? (2 marks)

46. Explain what may happen in a community with dishonest leaders. (3 marks)

47. Explain what interdependence means and give one example. (3 marks)

48. Using time words, write a short history of a school that opened in 1985 and built a library in 2000. (3 marks)

49. Give three rules for using safe school transport. (3 marks)

50. Explain why herding communities live in sparsely populated areas. (3 marks)

51. State three duties of the governor. (3 marks)

52. Describe how you would show a river, a lake and a mountain on a map with a key. (3 marks)

53. Explain how a village elder can help two neighbours who quarrel about a fence. (4 marks)

54. Give three benefits of industries to a county. (3 marks)

55. Explain why traditional culture is important. (3 marks)

56. Give four instructions to guide a visitor from the school gate to the office using cardinal points. The office is 50 steps north and then 20 steps east of the gate. (4 marks)

57. State three qualities of a good citizen in school and give an example for each. (3 marks)

58. Name two artefacts made by communities in Kenya. (2 marks)

59. Explain what may happen if people cut down all the trees on a mountain. (3 marks)

60. Name two places where you can find information about your school's history. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — On the right of the school
   East is on the right when north is at the top.

2. D — Wards
   Sub-counties are divided into wards.

3. D — Indian Ocean
   Kenya's coast is on the Indian Ocean.

4. C — Kilifi
   Kilifi lies along the coast.

5. A — Nairobi
   Nairobi County contains Kenya's capital city.

6. C — Relative location
   Relative location compares a place with its neighbours.

7. C — On high land
   Rivers start on high land and flow to lower land.

8. A — Planting trees along its banks
   Trees hold the soil and keep the water clean.

9. D — Move animals to find water and grass
   Grass and water become scarce, so herders move.

10. D — Malaria
   Mosquitoes that spread malaria breed in standing water.

11. B — Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
   Planting and harvesting depend on rain and dry weather.

12. C — A cloud with lines falling from it
   Falling lines under a cloud show rain.

13. B — Reporting anyone who damages it
   Reporting damage helps protect the place.

14. D — Food or money from selling food
   The tailor depends on the farmer for food.

15. A — Farmers grow the food they eat
   Everyone needs food, including nurses and doctors.

16. B — Linear
   Linear means in a line.

17. A — Bao
   Bao is a board game with seeds.

18. C — Instructions on what we should and should not do
   Rules guide behaviour.

19. D — First, then, later, today
   Time words link events in order.

20. A — Tourism
   Tourism serves visitors.

21. C — Teaching
   Teaching is work done to help others.

22. A — Good roads and nearby workers
   Transport and workers matter.

23. D — Stay with the group and not touch machines
   Safety rules protect visitors.

24. D — They provide jobs
   Industries employ people.

25. A — To protect a person from harm
   PPE protects the wearer.

26. B — Sharing tasks in a group
   Cooperation is working well with others.

27. C — Return it to the owner
   Returning shows honesty.

28. A — The school is safe and orderly
   Good citizens make a peaceful school.

29. A — A member of a country or community with rights and duties
   Citizens belong to a community and have rights and duties.

30. B — To learn in a safe place
   Learning safely is a right.

31. D — A disagreement or quarrel
   A conflict is a disagreement.

32. C — The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act
   Kenyan law protects children.

33. D — Cutting a girl's private parts, which is harmful and illegal
   FGM harms girls and is against the law.

34. D — Poverty and harmful beliefs
   Poverty and harmful beliefs are causes.

35. A — The larger number of votes
   Majority means more than others.

36. B — The people or parts that make up the group
   Composition means the members that make up a group.

37. B — Voting for leaders
   Voting is part of participating.

38. B — Sharing food aid equally and recording it
   Fairness and honesty are good leadership.

39. B — Every five years
   General elections are held every five years.

40. A — The county assembly
   The assembly must approve them.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: People can fish in the lake and sell the fish. People on the dry plain can keep cattle and goats. Both bring food and income. The county can also use both for tourism.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 25 pupils voted. Maria won.
   Working / marking points: 14 + 9 + 2 = 25. 14 is more than 9, so Maria won. 1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the winner, 1 mark for showing working.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They bring classmates' ideas and complaints to meetings, tell the class what was decided, and help solve small problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say no loudly, go to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A lake is a large area of water with land around it. A river is water flowing along a channel to a lake or ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Resources are wasted, people lose trust, and people quarrel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Interdependence means people depend on and help each other. For example, a farmer grows food and a trader sells it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example, 1 mark for showing both sides need each other.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: The school was opened in 1985. Later, in 2000, a library was built. Today, pupils read books in the library.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dates, 1 mark for order, 1 mark for time words.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use only transport approved by the school and parents, do not take lifts from strangers, and do not board overloaded vehicles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: The land is dry, so it cannot support many farms. Herders move with their animals to look for water and grass. So only a few people stay in one place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lead the county executive, present the budget and plans, and represent the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wavy blue line for a river, a blue patch for a lake and a brown triangle or brown shading for a mountain, with a key that explains them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct symbol described, up to 3.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to both, be fair, help them to talk and agree, and encourage them to forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give jobs, they buy farmers' produce, and they pay taxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives identity, teaches values, and brings people together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start at the gate. Walk 50 steps north. Turn to face east. Walk 20 steps east to the office.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear instruction with the right direction.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty: returning lost items. Respect: greeting teachers. Responsibility: doing class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with example.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: A kiondo basket and a soapstone carving. Accept clay pots, beaded jewellery or wooden stools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each artefact.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain may wash away the soil. Rivers may dry up. There may be landslides or floods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct result.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: The headteacher or teachers, and the school records or log book. Accept old photographs or elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each source.
